summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, HIT antibody positivity, and PTSD was readmitted two weeks after discharge for recurrent facial swelling and severe right thigh pain. She developed a large right groin hematoma following multiple failed femoral line attempts while on warfarin, which was held due to an elevated INR. The hematoma caused significant pain and sensory changes but remained stable on serial ultrasounds, requiring no surgical intervention. She was treated with IV Dilaudid, diazepam, and diphenhydramine for pain and anxiety. Due to worsening facial swelling and SVC occlusion, she underwent successful port stripping and SVC recanalization with angioplasty. Anticoagulation was transitioned from argatroban to warfarin with a fondaparinux bridge. A urine culture showed Klebsiella, deemed a contaminant, and antibiotics were discontinued. Her hemoglobin improved from a nadir of 22.2 to 24.5 without transfusion. She was discharged on a Dilaudid taper, warfarin, fondaparinux, and outpatient instructions including INR monitoring and discussion of IV iron with her PCP.
